sentences.text: Magnosaurus translates to 'large lizard' and represents a theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of England.
Estimates suggest this animal could reach four meters in length, stand one and a half meters high, and weigh two hundred kilograms.
The original specimens consisted of lower jaw fragments, back and tail bones, parts of the right hip bone, internal casts of the thigh and shin bones, and possibly belonged to a young individual.
This creature is classified within the superfamily Megalosauroidea and belongs to the family Megalosauridae.
In 2012, researchers Carrano and colleagues placed Magnosaurus in the subfamily Afrovenatorinae.
Later revisions classify it as a basal tetanuran within Megalosauroidea, possibly a Megalosaurid and Eustreptospondylinae.
Magnosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 175 to 170 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Specifically, it inhabited the Bajocian stage, between 170.9 and 168.6 million years ago.
Rauhut (2003) debated that Magnosaurus and Eustreptospondylus were the same genus, citing shared features like an expanded dentary tip and enlarged third dentary tooth.
Rauhut (2003) placed Magnosaurus with Eustreptospondylus due to similarities in the dentary and an elongated outer tooth.
